extension.news: v1.0.10: Repo now serves Video Add-ons Setup (script.tony7bones.video)

extension.description: Installs repositories and add-ons for a personal Kodi build.
extension.news: Trims the Estuary home menu to TV, Add-ons, Favourites, Weather. (v1.0.22 added Kodi home + sources directories to File Manager. v1.0.21 skipped optional dependencies — no more pulling Google Drive / cloud resolvers you didn't ask for. The installer now matches Kodi's own behaviour and resolves only required dependencies; optional imports stay on-demand. (v1.0.20 made Setup remove itself after a successful run. v1.0.19 stopped pinning Setup to the home screen and made the MOD V2 patch manual-only. v1.0.18 added the end-of-setup restart prompt.)

extension.summary: Apply tony7bones logo and breadcrumb fixes to Estuary MOD V2
extension.description: Replaces the MOD V2 logo with the standard Estuary wordmark (vendor_logo.png) and restores section labels in the top bar. Run this after installing or updating skin.estuary.modv2. Safe to re-run — original files are backed up once and never overwritten.

extension.summary: Install video add-ons from the Tony.7.Bones repos
extension.description: Pick which video add-ons to install (POV, The Loop, Sports HD, Umbrella). Each is installed with its full dependency closure, resolved live from the repositories already on this box, then enabled so it works straight away. Run the main Tony.7.Bones Setup first so the source repositories are present.
extension.news: The Loop's Dailymotion is installed-but-disabled (durable across Loop updates) instead of excluded. Dailymotion is installed as The Loop's normal required dependency — so The Loop's dependency check is satisfied with no broken flag and no required-dependency lock — then disabled at the end of the run so it never actually runs. Because it stays installed, this survives Loop auto-updates with no re-patching. Only Dailymotion is disabled; The Loop, POV and Sports HD stay enabled and browse normally. Still stamps origins and skips optional dependencies (no Google Drive / cloud resolvers).
